rule: A role is a placeholder that gets no permissions until a card is assigned. The cards assigned will define page access and read write permissions. It's that simple and there are to be zero exceptions to this rule. (Lutan, 2026-10-24)
note: Counts are lines in src/**/*.ts(x) matching `pattern`, taken from origin/main at baselineCommit. They may only go down. Read by scripts/check-hard-coded-security.mjs and, later, by the Hidden security screen. cards-grants-app was changing src/lib/permissions/cards.ts at the same time: if a count disagrees because it landed first, merge origin/main and re-baseline downward. Since 2026-10-24 (docs/decisions/2026-10-24-ratchet-counts-rules-not-mentions.md) a count is of CODE: comments are blanked before matching and the functions under diagnostics are blanked too; baselines were re-measured that way, downward only. 2026-10-25 (claude/security-db-half, migration 0259): the roles-scope-people entry was REMOVED from this list, not reduced to zero — the database half deleted the last clauses that read roles.scope_residents / scope_contacts / scope_photos / scope_clinical / opens_app, and the three comments that anchored the entry now describe history rather than a live rule. Mechanisms went from 6 to 5. roles.sees_login_emails was dropped, column and plumbing together. Admin is unchanged and is still outsideTheCardSystem below.

diagnostics.reason: tileBlock() evaluates the existing rules (OUTSIDE_REGISTRY, routes.ts) only to REPORT which one refused a held card, so the Who-does-what screen can name it. It creates no rule and grants or denies nothing. Surfacing hidden security is the point (Lutan: "I can't fix it if I can't see it"). The exemption is by function, not by file or directory: a rule added anywhere else in tiles.ts, or in src/lib/permissions/, is still counted. Added with #915 cards-grants-app.

survivesTheTest.what: The order roles are listed on an admin screen
survivesTheTest.why: ordering only; nothing keyed by it changes what a card does or whether it shows

mechanisms.name: canUseBills
mechanisms.effect: REMOVED 2026-10-25: the scopes.clinical === own_clinic clause is gone; what remains is three card-derived activity checks (stock.delivery, medical.visits at edit, maintenance.bills). The baseline counts callers of the function, which is not a rule.

mechanisms.name: page rules (route registry)
mechanisms.effect: NOT a breach, corrected 2026-10-25. A page rule says 'this page needs activity X at level L'; whether a role holds X is can() over role_permissions, which since 0257 the database computes from card_grants alone. The only non-card test inside routes.ts was route.scope (the role's clinical column), removed in this PR. Every entry now consults card-derived permissions only. The count is the number of pages, not the number of rules.
mechanisms.note: The planner's brief counted 55; this file has 45 path entries at the baseline commit. Recorded as found.

mechanisms.name: OUTSIDE_REGISTRY
mechanisms.effect: All six pages now obey the rule (REMOVED 2026-10-25): /residents asks resident.record at read, /bills asks canUseBills (card-derived), /operations and /management ask opensAnyIn (card-derived); /assistant and /my were already correct and untouched.

mechanisms.name: cardTile() silent drop
mechanisms.effect: REMOVED 2026-10-25: cardTile() still draws no tile for a page the role cannot open (a tile would invent access), but cardsWithoutTile() names every such card and the home says so in plain words. Nothing is dropped silently.

mechanisms.name: opensAnyIn
mechanisms.effect: NOT a breach, corrected 2026-10-25: any route in the section the role can open, so it inherits canOpen(), which is card-derived once route.scope is gone. Tracked, not counted as a mechanism.

outsideTheCardSystem.what: Admin: access to everything, hard-coded. src/lib/permissions/can.ts returns true for a login whose roles.is_admin is set before it looks at any cell or card.
outsideTheCardSystem.why: Lutan, 2026-10-25, asked directly: "I am happy for admin access = all to be hard coded." and "It should sit outside the card system." The invariant: "Admin always has access to everything. No matter what cards exist or don't exist." Measured on production 2026-10-25: Admin holds NO cards, so that one line is the only source of Admin's access; removing it would lock the only administrator out of Settings > Who does what, the screen needed to give Admin cards again. A one-way door.
rules: Admin is outside the card system, not an exception inside it.
It is not debt: no baseline, no count, never ratcheted.
It is not a precedent: Admin only, all-or-nothing.

databaseHalf.what: The database no longer reads any role column to grant or deny anything (migration 0259, docs/decisions/2026-10-25-security-database-half.md).
databaseHalf.why: This registry counts lines in src/**/*.ts(x) only, so a database rule can never appear in it. The database half is recorded here so nobody concludes from a green run that the database was ever covered.
databaseHalf.listGrew: The brief named eleven. Reading the LIVE definitions rather than grepping for create-or-replace found four more: holds_app_role() (which had already moved from roles.opens_app to r.key <> public_viewer), my_permissions(), photos_medical_only() and reassign_recurring_job(). sees_all_translations(), which the brief named, does not exist.
databaseHalf.measured: No losses. Every measured change was a role reading MORE: the role columns sat beside a card check and only ever subtracted. 33 widenings across five roles, 103 surfaces unchanged, Admin unchanged on every surface. Held in docs/card-access-faults.md for Card review 2.
databaseHalf.leftInPlace: roles.scope_residents, scope_clinical, scope_contacts, scope_photos and opens_app still EXIST as columns. Nothing reads them for access. Dropping them reaches a dozen check scripts and is its own PR.
